result.summary: Replaces the Boost.Test library with an in-tree C++ unit test runner and assertion framework implemented in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp}. The new framework implements expression decomposition to automatically log operand values on assertion failure while providing backward-compatible BOOST_* macro shims so existing tests run without modification. Boost.Test is completely removed from CMake, depends, Guix, and vcpkg build configurations.
result.problem: Boost.Test imposes external dependency maintenance costs in depends and Guix, hinders clang-tidy and IWYU adoption in test code, suffers from platform quirks like signal stack handling, and provides inconsistent assertion macros that often omit expression values on failure.
evidence: Author notes: 'Replacing Boost.Test as a runner helps us simplify depends and guix as well as use IWYU and clang-tidy within the tests more effectively.'
Addresses long-standing discussions on replacing Boost.Test tracked in issues #8670, #34666, and signal stack bugs like #36045.

enables: Migration of test files from BOOST_* compatibility shims to native CHECK and TEST_CASE macros.

result.scope_notes: Almost all touched files (over 160) are modified via a mechanical scripted-diff that updates include paths from boost test headers to test/util/framework.h. The core logic is concentrated in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp} and build scripts.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a commit to drop an unused Boost.Test workaround in Guix (contrib/guix/libexec/build_linux.sh), bringing touched files to 168.
result.card: This PR replaces the Boost.Test framework with an in-tree unit test runner and assertion library in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp}. The change eliminates Boost.Test as an external build dependency in depends, Guix, and vcpkg, improves static analysis support, and introduces expression decomposition for clearer test failure reports. Backward-compatible BOOST_* macro shims allow existing tests and in-flight PRs to compile without merge conflicts. Over 160 of the 168 files changed are mechanical header replacements performed by a scripted diff.

risk.why: Mistakes could break test compilation or false-fail unit test runs, but cannot affect node binaries or network behavior.
